frequency_question: How often does an executive nominee go from pending status to a confirmed floor vote within an 8-day window?
membership_rule: Includes all cabinet-level and major agency head nominations (such as FDA, EPA, Cabinet secretaries) pending on the Senate executive calendar where floor time is requested within an 8-day window. Excludes recess appointments and nominations withdrawn before consideration.

cases.name: Marty Makary or similar recent hypothetical agency heads (historical average)

provenance_note: claims 50 cases from only 5 named (10.0x); beyond 3.0x the skeleton is not carrying the estimate
coverage_note: 50 instances sampled across recent congressional calendars; estimated 10% proceed to an actual recorded floor vote within an 8-day unheralded window.
known_gaps: Senate floor schedules are highly idiosyncratic and depend on majority leadership priorities rather than uniform statistical baselines.
skeleton: Historically, high-profile agency nominations requiring Senate floor votes in a tightly constrained 8-day window without prior immediate scheduling signals happen rarely because Senate scheduling requires days of cloture motions and debate.
multiplier: Estimated ~5 relevant fast-tracked confirmations out of ~50 total pending executive calendar items in compressed windows over recent comparable congressional sessions.
validity_reason: Valid until the expiration of the current 119th Congress Senate rules and majority control dynamics.
